manual_notes: Stable provenance and source-independent card reconstruction are substantively implemented for a first SmashUp transfer family. The pinned rollout explicitly limits verified coverage and lists remaining cross-game/deferred migrations. The selected broad domain guarantees were not fully established across the advertised boundaries; checked tasks document an initial rollout, not proof of universal acceptance.
rationale: Correct task group and real first-batch implementation. Broader event self-sufficiency, presentation-descriptor and deferred-state requirements exceed the traced evidence. Design allows staged migration, so this is unresolved full-scope completion rather than abandonment.

sources.observed_facts: Inspected sessionContext.ts actor normalization and SmashUp objectProvenance.ts reference/provenance/reconstruction/transfer event implementation.
Pinned production helper stores uid, owner provenance, default destination, controller context and can reconstruct a card without the live original.
CARD_TRANSFERRED prefers objectRef reconstruction, but legacy fallback can still derive owner from fromPlayerId when objectRef/ownerId absent.
The rollout explicitly restricts verified work to engine session seam and first SmashUp provenance/deferred families; other games and remaining high-risk families are described as not yet migrated.

limitations: Static review only; no tests were executed or deployed behavior independently verified.
review_depth: Read full specification, design, checked tasks and rollout inventory; inspected actor/provenance implementation, pinned reducer fallback and interaction system snapshot/display fields. Broad cross-game acceptance was not exhaustively traced. Tests were not run.
